message:
Just an update, after complaining to Governor O'Malley I finally got the PSC final ruling.  They dismissed my complaint and gave me an opportunity for judicial review. I may or may not pursue it.

The bottom line is the process was good for me in that T-NETIX did some serious lying in their responses.  At the same time I had that complaint I also had one at the FCC.  In that complaint they lied and told the FCC that it was no additional issues to the PSC complaint.  I found this out when I got the formal with the PSC.

This morning I e-mailed Commissioner Copps at FCC to find out what is the penalty for lying to the FCC?  and would I be permitted to have my complaint heard again.  I will wait for an answer.

Next, after this I reported to the FCC Enforcement Dept that T-NETIX gave me preferential treatment , the territorial manager instructed the customer service manager to increase my credit limit to $500 on each of my phone lines.
I never asked him to do this.  This is discrimination as far as the Telecommunication Act is concerned and a clear violation of the Act.

You can read about this in the supplement to my complaint.  Go to MD PSC website and click on official filings.  Type in T-NETIX and hit go and you will see my complaint along with two supplements.

I also took the liberty of informing Mr. Elliot Schlanger of MD DBM of this and about T-NETIX lying in the PSC complaint.  This is the biggy, a response came to me by way of Office of the Attorney with a cc to Schlanger.  Rather then answer me directly they claimed that they would wait for the outcome of the PSC and FCC.

When you read this on PSC website(about my complaint) then you know that they realize what is coming down the pike.

I feel that Verizon is a part of the conspiracy with T-NETIX, Evercom and CBS.

Hope that complaints go to FCC and MD DBM when people read this, its not fair to everyone that have posted here and been a victim.
